queue_items.claim: The rival's rejection rests on the Selah at web:Ps.89.4, which the book's binding policy bars from boundary-driver work.

The mark itself is real and correctly located -- WEB 'Selah.' at Ps.89.4 = סֶֽלָה at oshb:Ps.89.5 (Ps 89 is shift+1) -- and observed_substrate_signals[2] tiers it correctly as 'tier-3 corroboration', so the defect is confined to the rejected_alternative, where it does driver work. The row's own book-order neighbor argues the same mark to the stricter standard (M8-Ps-277: 'this unit's own content ... is untouched by that closing mark'), which is the internal inconsistency. Not load-bearing on the span: the front edge is the maskil-le-Ethan title, מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל לְאֵיתָ֥ן הָֽאֶזְרָחִֽי (oshb:Ps.89.1, byte tier; web:Ps.89.0 = oshb:Ps.89.1), a tier-1 opener, and the back edge has the independent voice shift to direct praise at web:Ps.89.5 that M8-Ps-277 argues. queue_items.grounds: device_notes states the sequence '(darkness, blood, frogs, insects, hail, locusts, and the death of the firstborn) covers 7 of the traditional plagues and omits the livestock-pestilence and boils'. With exactly two omissions named the arithmetic must close at ten, so 7 is one short on the row's own terms. The count OBJECT is also unnamed and out of scope: 'the traditional plagues' is an Exodus-scoped set that the Ps-scoped staged tools cannot sweep - the section 11 OL-c28 class, where a claim must be scoped explicitly or dropped. The trailing clause 'omits the livestock-pestilence and boils material present in this psalm's own catalogue by their absence' is self-contradictory as written. Not load-bearing: device_notes itself labels the observation 'texture, not boundary authority for these rows', and neither of the row's seams rests on it.
